The optional PC companion reconnects when TCP works but ADB does not respond. It manages a separate ADB server and leaves other ADB work alone.
Waiting for network recovery · retries automatically
Connect Tailscale on this phone first, then start ADB. Run the command below from your computer. A new host remains unauthorized until you allow shell access here.
This app’s listener is bound to the verified Tailscale VPN interface and address. It does not change Android’s wireless debugging setting or existing ADB listeners.
Root is required to start the isolated ADB process. Access is requested automatically when the app opens.
This build supports the verified Android 16 adbd binary on SM-S948Q and KernelSU with no-new-privileges support. It stops if either security boundary is unavailable.
ADB shell network operations run in an isolated network namespace. Normal apps retain their own network access. Standard Android wireless debugging can be turned off independently.
Manage saved Tailscale IP permissions. Turning off shell access also revokes root access. Turning on root access also enables shell access.
Every connection starts as the Android shell user. The su command works only for a connected Tailscale IP explicitly allowed here. Changing access restarts this app’s private ADB listener.
Starts Tail ADB after Android finishes booting, including a software reboot. If root is unavailable, startup stops safely and the app shows an error instead of retrying in a loop.
